function: Camera-aided beam prediction: LSTM predicts the optimal base-station codebook beam index from sequences of transmitter bounding boxes or masks extracted at distributed camera nodes (pp. 4, 9-10).
system: Single-antenna mobile transmitter; base station with three 16-element ULAs (60 GHz), 64-beam codebook; two distributed RGB-camera nodes; no RIS (pp. 4, 12-13).
method: Pre-trained YOLOv7 (COCO) extracts boxes and masks; FCNN regresses transmitter location from receive power; LSTM predicts beam index from 5-frame sequences; supervised, Adam, cross-entropy (pp. 6, 8-10, 14).
data_channel: Measured DeepSense 6G scenario 41: real 60 GHz receive-power vectors, RGB images and GPS; 2991 and 5476 sequences for units 2 and 3 (pp. 12-13).
test_conditions: Same scenario, daytime; sequences split 70:20:10 into training, validation, test (p. 13); separate datasets per node (p. 14); accuracy broken down by distance and object count (pp. 17-19).
baselines: Classical: none. Learned: FCNN on bounding boxes, LeNet CNN on masks; position-aided FCNN for transmitter identification (pp. 9, 11, 16).
metrics: Top-1, top-2, top-3 beam accuracy; achievable rate; comparative and association accuracy of transmitter identification; inference time in ms (pp. 14-17).
complexity: Inference time: YOLOv7 29.5 ms per frame on T4 GPU, LSTM beam prediction 0.37 to 1.46 ms, transmitter identification 0.037 ms; YOLOv7 has 37.5 M parameters (pp. 11-12).
openness: Uses public DeepSense 6G scenario 41 [28]; no link to the authors' own code (p. 12).
q1_support: p. 12: "DeepSense 6G is a comprehensive real-world dataset specifically designed for sensing-aided wireless communication applications." Scenario 41 is measured data collected on McAllister Ave., Tempe (p. 13).
q2_support: p. 13: "split into training, validation, and testing categories with a ratio of 70:20:10". Held-out part of the same scenario; Figs. 13 and 17 break down the same test data; nighttime is only anticipated (pp. 13-14).
q3_support: p. 16: "the LSTM model that takes bounding boxes as input achieves better top-1, top-2, and top-3 beam prediction accuracies than the corresponding FCNN model". Learned baselines only; no non-learned beam baseline is evaluated.
q4_support: p. 11: "takes about 1-2 ms per prediction when executed on an Nvidia RTX A5000 GPU". Table 1 (p. 12) lists inference latency per model; YOLOv7 has 37.5 million parameters (p. 12).
q5_support: p. 12: "we employ the DeepSense 6G dataset [28]". Public dataset of measured mmWave and camera data; the paper gives no link for its own code.
notes: Title on page 1 matches the DOI. Area 3: the learned model predicts the base-station beam; the camera sensing is out-of-band and does not serve the beams, so area 5 was not chosen, reviewer to confirm. YOLOv7 is pre-trained on COCO (p. 6); the authors train the FCNN and LSTM models. Nearest-neighbor tracking is not learned. The exhaustive-search remark on p. 16 is an overhead statement, not a measured comparison.
